extracted.intended_audience: public company legal, compliance, securities officers, audit committees, and general counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Practical legal and compliance guidance for public companies (large accelerated filers, accelerated filers, smaller reporting companies, emerging growth companies) on steps to take while the SEC’s climate disclosure rules are stayed. Focuses on disclosures, internal controls, governance, audit engagement, benchmarking, and cross‑jurisdictional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue responding to SEC staff comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC staff is likely to continue issuing comment letters on companies’ current climate-related disclosures, including comments based on the SEC’s 2010 guidance on climate change disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume the stay ends staff scrutiny; maintain readiness to respond to comment letters. Track and promptly address SEC staff inquiries even while the final rules are stayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure consistency between public sustainability statements and SEC filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC staff often compares climate-related statements in company filings with climate-related information made public by the company on its website or in other reports or publications. The staff has been issuing comments for years on discrepancies it believes exist between a company’s sustainability reports and its periodic reports filed with the SEC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review public climate-related statements (websites, sustainability reports, press releases) and reconcile them with SEC-filed disclosures to avoid discrepancies that could trigger staff comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess exposure to other jurisdictions' climate disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should consider whether they will be subject to climate disclosure rules proposed or adopted in other jurisdictions, and if so, begin the process of understanding such rules and their impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory applicable and emerging non‑U.S. and subnational requirements (e.g., EU rules, California statutes) and map differences to current reporting processes to identify gaps and compliance implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain focus on accuracy, controls, and third‑party assurance readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent the company is already making climate-related disclosures, including with respect to greenhouse gas (“GHG”) emissions, it should maintain its focus on ensuring consistency and accuracy in such reporting, including reviewing current controls and procedures designed to ensure the accuracy of such information and ability to obtain third-party assurance of the emissions disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review and strengthen data collection controls, internal procedures, and documentation so that reported climate metrics are defensible; evaluate options and preparedness for obtaining third‑party assurance of emissions data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark peer disclosures and investor expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: An awareness of public disclosures being made by peers in the same industry and similarly situated in terms of market capitalization, revenue and SEC filer status may serve as useful benchmarking should the climate disclosure rules come into effect and may inform institutional investor expectations in any case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect examples of peer disclosures to gauge market norms and investor expectations; use benchmarking to inform scope, granularity, and comparability of your disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate and formalize disclosure controls and board/committee review
rubrics_metrics.description: Many large public companies already have begun to implement disclosure controls and procedures relating to climate and other sustainability disclosures, including by subjecting these disclosures to disclosure committee and board level review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure climate disclosures are integrated into established disclosure controls and review cycles; document roles, responsibilities, and escalation paths (disclosure committees, audit committee, board) for climate-related reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess financial statement disclosure requirements for severe weather and other natural conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The new rules also impose new financial statement disclosure requirements regarding costs associated with “severe weather events” and “other natural conditions.” Companies and their audit committees may want to consider the financial implications of climate-related risks that are material to their businesses, how this new financial statement disclosure requirement could be implemented and what new internal controls might be necessary to help ensure compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit committees should evaluate the potential magnitude and accounting treatment of climate‑related costs, identify processes to capture such costs, and determine necessary controls and documentation for financial statement disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage auditors on design and testing of new or modified internal controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies can also consider initiating discussions with their auditors regarding their plans for complying with this aspect of the rules and regarding the design and testing of new or modified internal controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate early with external auditors to align on expectations for control design, testing timelines, and evidence needed for audited/assured climate metrics or financial statement impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare GHG emissions disclosures: identify, gather, synthesize, and consider service providers
rubrics_metrics.description: GHG emissions disclosures, if material, may be among the most burdensome of the requirements in the new rules. The stay on the final rules is an opportunity for those companies subject to such requirements ... to make progress in identifying, gathering, and synthesizing this information, and to consider engaging with service providers to assist with this effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map emissions sources, establish data‑collection processes, assemble teams and tools to synthesize inventory data, and evaluate third‑party service providers for data collection, assurance, or reporting support.

rubrics_metrics.name: For smaller or emerging companies: get up to speed and educate the board
rubrics_metrics.description: Accelerated filers, smaller reporting companies and emerging growth companies ... could well use the time afforded by the rules’ challenge to: get up to speed on the climate-related reporting and the obligations it would impose on the company, and if material, educate their boards of directors to facilitate the company’s development of corporate governance and risk management policies and procedures related to climate risk;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tailored briefings to boards, create simple governance frameworks, and set a roadmap for developing disclosure capabilities and risk management practices appropriate to company size and complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review competitor, industry leader, supplier, and end‑user disclosures if risks are material
rubrics_metrics.description: If climate-related risks are expected to be material, review climate-related disclosures that competitors, industry leaders, suppliers or end-users make;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform targeted review of stakeholder disclosures to understand relevant metrics, methodologies, and stakeholder expectations that could influence your own disclosure approach and materiality determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategize about information systems, processes and controls needed for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategize about the information systems, processes and controls that the company would need to implement if the rules come back into effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a concrete plan and timeline to implement or upgrade IT systems, data flows, internal controls, and governance processes necessary to produce required disclosures at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor litigation, timing, and plan for transition periods
rubrics_metrics.description: It appears the SEC is settling in for a long fight. ... It is likely the SEC will provide some transition period before the clock starts ticking again, although any such transition period will likely depend on the duration and result of the litigation, including which parts of the rules remain intact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track the litigation and regulatory developments closely; build flexible implementation plans that can accelerate or pause depending on court outcomes and any transition periods the SEC may announce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the stay to review and update current disclosures, controls and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: While the SEC has stayed the Final Rules, companies may take this opportunity to review their current climate-related disclosures, familiarize themselves with disclosure requirements to which they and their industry peers may become subject, and implement or update relevant controls and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the stay as an opportunity to remediate weaknesses, document practices, and implement incremental improvements so the organization is ready if and when obligations resume; consider engaging outside counsel or consultants for guidance.
